newsitem.title: PERU: Peru Jan-Feb trade gap falls 21 pct to $212 mln.
newsitem.headline: Peru Jan-Feb trade gap falls 21 pct to $212 mln.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell 21 percent in the first two months of the year to $212 million from $268 million in the same period last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Friday.

Earlier this week, government's official newspaper, El Peruano, reported the January-February trade gap was down 24 percent to $210 million from $275 in the same period last year. El Peruano cited "economic authorities" for its figures.

The central bank said in its weekly report that exports were $1.040 billion in the first two months, up 15.1 percent compared with the same period last year. Imports were $1.252 billion, up 6.9 percent on the same period last year.
Traditional exports -- including the oil, mining, agriculture and fishing sectors -- rose 7.8 percent to $723 million. Non-traditional exports rose 40.0 percent to $305 million.
Among imports, consumer goods fell 9.1 percent to $249 million, raw materials edged up 0.6 percent to $511 million, and capital goods imports gained 24.6 percent to $440 million.
Peru's trade deficit fell 9.0 percent in 1996 to $1.996 billion from $2.185 billion in 1995, according to the bank.
